studyGroups.title: Free English study groups for developers
studyGroups.seoTitle: Free English Study Groups for Devs
studyGroups.seoDescription: Practice English with other developers in small, free study groups. Join or start a group, pick a weekly tech topic and talk it through together.
studyGroups.intro: Most documentation, open-source discussion, conference talks and remote jobs in software happen in English. Reading it is a start; speaking it with confidence takes practice. This program helps developers practice together in small, friendly study groups.
studyGroups.joinCta: Join a free English study group
studyGroups.whyTitle: Why developers practice English in groups
studyGroups.whyIntro: Reading docs in English is one skill. Explaining a trade-off out loud in a code review or an interview is another, and it only improves when you speak. Studying alone with an app rarely gets you there. A small group that meets every week, talks about a technical topic everyone prepared, and lets each person make mistakes in front of friendly peers does.
why: Docs, release notes, RFCs and most answers to hard problems are written in English first.
Open-source projects, issue trackers and code reviews happen in English, so you can contribute and be understood.
International and remote teams hire people who can explain trade-offs, ask questions and run meetings in English.
Talking about real technical topics every week builds vocabulary and confidence faster than studying alone.
how: Sign in with Google and accept the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy.
Create a group with a name, a short public summary, rules and a meeting schedule, or ask to join an existing one with its access code.
The group owner approves each request, so only approved members open the board.
Members suggest videos, articles, books or podcasts; the owner picks the weekly topic by a random draw or a vote.
Meet on your own call and talk about it in English. Mistakes are part of the practice.
studyGroups.startText: You don't need to be a teacher to start a group. You need a few colleagues, a fixed time and a topic. Create the group here, write a short public summary and your rules, then share the access code with the people you want to invite: your team, your university class, or a community you already belong to. Members suggest videos, articles or talks during the week, and the board picks the next topic by a random draw or a vote. Meet on whatever call tool you already use.
studyGroups.groupsIntro: Each card shows the group's name and the summary its creator wrote. Ask the group for its access code before you request to join, or start your own group if none fits your schedule.

faq.a: Yes. Filipe Bojikian Rissi runs the program on his own site and charges nothing to create or join a group.

faq.q: What level of English do I need?
faq.a: Enough to follow a short technical video or article. Each group sets its own level and rules in its summary, so read it before you ask to join.

faq.q: Do groups have a teacher or a native speaker?
faq.a: Usually not. Groups are developers practicing with each other. Speaking regularly with peers on topics you know is the point.

faq.q: Where and when do groups meet?
faq.a: On the group's own call (Google Meet, Zoom, Discord or similar), at the time the owner sets. The schedule is part of each group's rules.

faq.q: Can I create a private group for my team or community?
faq.a: Yes. Only people with the access code can ask to join, and the owner approves each request.

faq.q: Why is the group app in English?
faq.a: Because the practice is in English. This page, the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy are also available in Portuguese.

From Google, your account identifier, your email address, whether it is verified and your name; never your profile picture. Then what you add: your display name, the groups you create and their icons (stored privately, without photo metadata, and shown only to members), your join requests, memberships, suggestions and votes, and your acceptance of the Terms and the Privacy Policy. Deleting is permanent and immediate. To keep you signed in we store only a hash of your session token, and when the platform admin deletes something or bans an account, a moderation log keeps a short label, the reason and the date, never the full content; a ban also keeps the account's Google ID and email while it lasts. Your email address is used only to send you service emails about your groups and requests (no marketing, and you can turn them off), sent through Amazon SES, with a record of each email kept for 30 days. Your email is never shown to other members or group owners. The Privacy Policy explains how long each item is kept and how to download your data or delete your account. Questions about the program, abuse reports and data requests go to groups@fbrissi.dev.
